title: Apple's iPhone 20 Projected to Feature Major Redesign and Cutting-Edge Technology for 2027 Launch
summary: Apple's iPhone 20 Projected to Feature Major Redesign and Cutting-Edge Technology for 2027 Launch
detailed: Apple is reportedly developing the 'iPhone 20' for a September 2027 release to mark the device's 20th anniversary with a major redesign.
Early leaks indicate a quad-curved, all-glass design developed in partnership with Samsung, solid-state haptic buttons, and an in-house third-generation modem.
The device is rumored to feature a second-generation 2-nanometer A21 chip, silicon anode battery technology for enhanced life, and vertically stacked DRAM.
Display sizes are anticipated to be approximately 6.41 inches and 6.96 inches, though advanced features like under-display Face ID remain subject to development timelines.
sentences: In 2017, Apple marked the 10th anniversary of the iPhone with the launch of the iPhone X, introducing the most significant redesign in the device’s history.
As the tech giant approaches the iPhone’s 20th anniversary, speculations hint at another groundbreaking redesign slated for release in September 2027.

Leaks have been accumulating in recent months, with insights from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman suggesting that Apple is already well into the development phase of what is expected to be the “iPhone 20.”
Early reports indicate that the new device will feature a quad-curved, all-glass design, where the display glass curves elegantly on all four sides to conceal the metal frame, creating a seamless look.
This ambitious design goal appears to be in partnership with Samsung, which is reportedly developing what is referred to as an “equal-depth quad-curved” display.

In terms of display technology, Apple has been exploring a new, brighter, and thinner OLED panel utilizing Color Filter on Encapsulation (COE), which was originally anticipated for the anniversary iPhone.
However, a recent report from UBI Research suggests that this technology may not make it to the iPhone lineup until 2029, raising questions about its inclusion in the upcoming model.
Aiming to further streamline the device’s aesthetics, Apple is reportedly testing under-display Face ID and camera technology.
While the company successfully introduced an under-display camera on the iPhone Duo’s inner screen, the quality of the imagery received criticism.
Whether an improved version will be ready by the expected launch date in fall 2027 remains to be determined.
In a move toward innovation, Apple might be implementing solid-state buttons that replace traditional mechanical ones.
These would provide haptic feedback through buttons integrated into the device’s frame, maintaining tactile responsiveness without any physical movement when pressed.
Apple is also advancing its in-house modem technology, striving to outperform Qualcomm’s offerings, particularly in speed and artificial intelligence functionalities.

The third-generation modem, expected to debut in 2027, aims to surpass Qualcomm’s capabilities, with the current C1 and C1X modems utilized in earlier iPhone models and the C2 now powering the iPhone 18 series.
Moreover, Apple is developing a custom image sensor designed to replace Sony’s current sensors used in iPhones.
Initial reports describe a working prototype employing LOFIC technology, which allows each pixel to capture varying amounts of light, potentially offering up to 20 stops of dynamic range.
The new models are anticipated to be powered by a second-generation 2-nanometer A21 chip, building on the existing A20 Pro found in the iPhone 18 Pro lineup.
Apple is also exploring advanced battery technology utilizing a silicon anode, which promises to enhance battery life without compromising size.
To further augment performance, Apple is rumored to be investigating vertically stacked DRAM technology to bolster memory bandwidth, which would also support on-device AI enhancements.
For the anniversary models, two size options are expected, slightly larger than the iPhone 18 Pro, with display sizes rumored to be approximately 6.41 inches and 6.96 inches.
As the anticipated release date is still several years ahead, it is essential to note that Apple’s plans may evolve continuously behind closed doors.
Features of such an ambitious nature often face delays, with the under-display Face ID technology having been rumored for several iterations now.
If the leaks hold true, the iPhone 20 could represent the most significant shift since 2017.
With these potential enhancements, many are eager to see if Apple can deliver on its ambitious promises, offering a compelling reason to wait for this landmark device.
In other news from the Apple ecosystem, rumors suggest that the iPhone’s Action button could soon be combined with the Camera Control feature starting next year.
Leakers have also speculated on a shortened iPhone design paired with a new iOS layout, keeping current width while reducing height.
Additionally, Apple is reportedly refining its approach to developing upcoming versions of iOS and macOS, aiming for a more efficient process across its software platforms.
